loginGuide.heading: Choose the right login
loginGuide.intro: Each kind of CodeAlgo Academy account has its own login, so parents, teachers, school leaders, and students each land in a space built for them. Pick the option above that matches the account you created. Not sure which one that is? Use the guide below.

items.title: Admin
items.body: For school, district, and program leaders who run an organization on CodeAlgo. Log in to manage users and roles, assign licenses, and oversee student accounts across your organization.

items.title: Parent or guardian
items.body: Log in to your Parent Hub to add children, set parental permissions and daily screen time limits, and follow each child's progress, achievements, and the skills they are mastering.

items.title: Teacher
items.body: Log in to your classroom dashboard to add students, assign content, monitor progress, reset student passwords, and print student login cards.

items.title: Student
items.body: Students play and learn at play.codealgoacademy.com. Use the username and password your parent or teacher created for you, or scan the QR code on your student login card.

tips.title: Forgot your password?
tips.body: Select "Forgot password" on your login form, enter your email address, and we will send you a link to reset it.

tips.title: Student can't sign in?
tips.body: The parent or teacher who set up the account can reset the password from their dashboard. QR codes on printed login cards keep working even if the username or password changes.

tips.title: Using the wrong login?
tips.body: Teachers, parents, and admins each log in from their own page. If you pick the wrong one, we will tell you which login page your account belongs to.

tips.title: Which devices work?
tips.body: CodeAlgo runs in any modern web browser on desktops, laptops, Chromebooks, tablets, and phones, so you can log in from home or school.

tips.title: Switching between school and home?
tips.body: Progress is saved to the student's account, so they can log in at school, keep playing at home, and pick up right where they left off.

tips.title: On a shared computer?
tips.body: Log out when you finish so the next person can sign in to their own account and every child's progress stays in the right place.

signupGuide.heading: What you get with each account
signupGuide.intro: CodeAlgo Academy teaches coding through a game-based world where every lesson is a level and every project is a quest. Choose the account that matches how you will use CodeAlgo.

items.title: Parent or guardian
items.body: Create accounts for your children and manage them from one Parent Hub. Set parental permissions and daily screen time limits, then follow each child's progress, achievements, and the skills they are mastering.

items.title: Teacher
items.body: Set up your classroom in minutes. Add students with single sign-on through Clever or Google Classroom, or add them by hand, then assign content, monitor progress, and print login cards with QR codes for younger students.

items.title: Student
items.body: Learn block coding, Python, math, and AI literacy through quests and challenges that adapt to your level. Your progress saves automatically, so you can pick up right where you left off.

steps: Enter your name, email address, and a password. Teachers also add their school name.
Parents add each child, create their login, and choose parental permissions and screen time. Teachers add their students and set up their classroom.
Start playing and learning right away, and follow progress from your dashboard.
signupGuide.tipsHeading: Good to know before you sign up

tips.title: Try it free
tips.body: A free trial lets you explore the platform before you choose a monthly or annual plan, and you can cancel your subscription at any time.

tips.title: Works on the devices you have
tips.body: CodeAlgo runs in any modern web browser on desktops, laptops, Chromebooks, tablets, and phones.

tips.title: Built for young learners
tips.body: Parents set permissions and screen time for their children, and our privacy practices are designed to comply with COPPA.

tips.title: Signing up a whole school?
tips.body: If you are bringing CodeAlgo to a school, district, or charter network, talk to us about classroom rostering, standards-aligned curriculum, and licensing for your organization.
